front.title: Proposed Extensions to the FLAC Standard

abstract.t: This document specifies extensions to the Free Lossless Audio Codec (FLAC) format defined in RFC 9639 . These additions specify:

ol.li: A new metadata block (STREAMINFO_EXTENSION, block type 7) supporting 64-bit IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point sample rates, up to 256 audio channels, standard WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE channel masks, extended bit depths up to 128 bits per sample, and explicit sample format indicators (integer PCM and IEEE 754 32-bit floating-point PCM).
An extended frame header operating in either Compact (8-bit payload) or Full (128-bit payload) mode, accompanied by deliberate backward-incompatibility signaling in legacy frame header fields.

An extended entropy coding method, PARTITIONED_RICE3 (type code 0b10), employing 7-bit Rice parameters and 7-bit raw escape bit lengths to accommodate residuals of ultra-high bit depths (up to 128 bits per sample).

A native IEEE 754 single-precision (32-bit) floating-point sample coding architecture utilizing dual subframes per audio channel, encompassing Dynamic Positional Alignment (DPA) and two's complement Fallback modes.
A new subframe type, PACKED (type code 0b000010), providing adaptive-width bit-packed storage for lower-order mantissa bits and raw float outlier samples.

section.name: Conventions and Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Deliberate Incompatibility and Signaling Strategy
section.t: Because extended streams may contain floating-point audio, non-integer sample rates, channel configurations up to 256 channels, or extended subframe payloads, feeding such streams to legacy RFC 9639 decoders would produce severe acoustic damage or decoder crashes.
This specification adopts a two-tier deliberate breaking strategy:

ol.li: Stream-Level Incompatibility: The STREAMINFO block signals the presence of STREAMINFO_EXTENSION by setting its bits_per_sample field to 0b00000 (representing 1 bit per sample). In , bit depths below 4 bits per sample are reserved and illegal. Compliant decoders MUST refuse to decode the stream upon encountering this value.

Frame-Level Incompatibility: The legacy frame header fields for sample rate, channel assignment, and bit depth are simultaneously set to previously forbidden or reserved codes (sample_rate = 0b1111, channel_assignment = 0b1111, bits_per_sample = 0b011). Furthermore, the frame header extension bytes are inserted immediately before the frame header CRC-8, causing legacy decoders seeking a CRC-8 at the legacy offset to encounter bit-shifted data and fail validation immediately.

section.name: Block Identification and Placement
section.t: The STREAMINFO_EXTENSION metadata block is identified by block type indicator 7 in the 7-bit metadata block header:

tr.td: 1 if this is the last metadata block, 0 otherwise

section.t: If present in a FLAC stream, the STREAMINFO_EXTENSION block MUST immediately follow the STREAMINFO block (i.e., at metadata block index 1). A stream MUST NOT contain more than one STREAMINFO_EXTENSION block.

section.name: Signaling in STREAMINFO
section.t: The presence of the STREAMINFO_EXTENSION block MUST be indicated in the preceding STREAMINFO block by encoding the 5-bit bits_per_sample field as 0b00000 (meaning 1 bit per sample).

If the channel count is higher than STREAMINFO's capacity (greater than 8 channels), STREAMINFO MUST store 0b000 bits (representing 1 channel). Otherwise, STREAMINFO and STREAMINFO_EXTENSION MUST both store the same channel count.
STREAMINFO's sample rate MUST be a rounded integer version of the STREAMINFO_EXTENSION sample rate (capped at 1,048,575 = 2^20 - 1 for higher rates).

section.name: Block Syntax and Bit Layout
section.t: The payload of the STREAMINFO_EXTENSION block is exactly 128 bits (16 octets) in length:

tr.td: 64 bits representing sample rate in Hz in IEEE 754 binary64 format
8 bits for (number of channels) - 1 (values 0..255 for 1..256 channels)
32 bits for standard WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE channel mask ( Section 8.6.2)
3 bits reserved for channel bitmap use case hints; MUST be 0b000
2 bits indicating whether to ignore channel mask; MUST be 0b00
4 bits: 0b0000 = integer PCM, 0b0001 = float PCM ( single precision)
7 bits for (bit depth) - 1 (values 0..127 for 1..128 bits per sample)
8 bits reserved for future development; MUST be 0b00000000

li.t: Sample Rate (64 bits): Sample rate in Hz represented in the standard binary64 format (double).

ul.li: Special numbers (subnormal numbers, positive zero, negative zero, infinities, and NaNs) and negative values are strictly FORBIDDEN.
The sample rate MAY be 0.0 (all 64 bits zero) to indicate that the information is only stored in STREAMINFO.

ol.li: Channel Count Minus 1 (8 bits): Encodes (number of channels) - 1. Values range from 0 (1 channel) to 255 (256 channels).
Channel Mask (32 bits): Standard 32-bit channel position mask conforming to the WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE specification as described in Section 8.6.2 of .

Special Mask Hints (3 bits): Reserved for hinting special use cases of the channel bitmap (e.g., standard stereo vs. headphone stereo). All values are currently reserved; encoders MUST set these bits to 0b000 and decoders MUST ignore them.

Ignore Mask Flag (2 bits): Indicates whether the decoder should ignore the WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE bits and use another custom channel mask. All values are currently reserved; encoders MUST set these bits to 0b00 and decoders MUST ignore them.

li.t: Sample Format (4 bits): An enumeration defining sample arithmetic:

ul.li: Other values are reserved for future development.

ol.li: Bits Per Sample Minus 1 (7 bits): Encodes (bit depth) - 1. If the sample format is float PCM, the bit depth MUST be 32 (encoded as value 31).
Reserved (8 bits): Reserved for future development. Encoders MUST set these bits to zero. Decoders MUST reject streams containing non-zero bits in this field.

section.name: Parameter Resolution and Compatibility Rules
section.t: When STREAMINFO_EXTENSION is present:

ol.li: New decoders MUST replace the corresponding legacy info from the STREAMINFO block with every valid piece of information from STREAMINFO_EXTENSION, and ignore the invalid ones.
If the sample_rate field in STREAMINFO_EXTENSION is 0.0, or contains a forbidden IEEE 754 special representation, the decoder MUST fall back to the sample_rate stored in STREAMINFO.
Only the extension header stream parameters are considered during audio decoding when the extension is present.

section.name: Signaling in the Legacy Frame Header
section.t: The encoder MUST use the extended frame header if and only if STREAMINFO_EXTENSION is present.
To ensure legacy decoders reject the frame, the legacy frame header fields MUST be set to the following indicator values:

Uncommon sample rates (sample rate hint codes 12, 13, and 14 requiring trailing octets) MUST NOT be used together with the frame header extension. Uncommon sample rates are deprecated; the frame extension MUST be used instead.

section.name: Format Selection (Compact vs. Full)
section.t: Bit 0 of byte 3 of the legacy frame header (raw_header[3] & 0x01), which was defined as a reserved zero-bit in , indicates the extension format:

ul.li: 0: Compact Mode. The extension payload is 8 bits (1 octet). Audio parameters (sample rate, channel count, channel mask, bit depth, and sample format) are inherited from STREAMINFO_EXTENSION.
1: Full Mode. The extension payload is 128 bits (16 octets), explicitly defining all stream parameters inline.

section.name: Framing and CRC-8 Coverage
section.t: The extension bits MUST immediately follow the main frame header bits (the frame/sample number and any blocksize hint) and directly precede the frame header CRC-8.
The frame header CRC-8 covers the extension bits as well as the preceding header bytes.

section.name: Compact Mode Syntax
section.t: In Compact Mode, the extension payload is 8 bits (1 octet):

tr.td: 0 = Dynamic Positional Alignment (DPA) mode, 1 = Fallback mode

section.name: Full Mode Syntax
section.t: In Full Mode, the extension payload is 128 bits (16 octets):

tr.td: 64 bits IEEE 754 binary64 sample rate in Hz (forbidden values trigger fallback)
32 bits standard WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE channel mask ( Section 8.6.2)
7 bits for (bit depth) - 1 (MUST be 31 for float PCM)
0 = Dynamic Positional Alignment (DPA) mode, 1 = Fallback mode

section.name: Inter-channel Decorrelation Descriptors
section.t: The interpretation of the 3-bit inter-channel decorrelation mode descriptor ID depends on the active channel configuration and channel mask.
For standard 2-channel stereo (SPEAKER_FRONT_LEFT | SPEAKER_FRONT_RIGHT, or channel mask 0x00000003):
For all other channel configurations, all 3-bit values other than 0b000 (Independent channels) are currently reserved for future multi-channel decorrelation schemes.

section.name: Method Type Allocation
section.t: Section 9.2.7 of defines the 2-bit residual coding method field. The value 0b10 was previously reserved. This specification allocates 0b10 as PARTITIONED_RICE3:

section.name: Coding Syntax and Parameters
section.t: PARTITIONED_RICE3 expands the Rice parameter and unencoded escape bit fields:

tr.td: 1 <= raw_bits <= 127: Unencoded signed two's complement width

section.name: Escape Mechanism and Raw Sample Coding
section.t: If the 7-bit Rice parameter read for a partition is strictly less than 127, the partition residual samples are decoded using signed Rice coding with parameter k.
If the Rice parameter equals 127:

ol.li: The decoder reads a 7-bit unsigned integer raw_bits.
The decoder reads each residual sample in the partition as an unencoded signed two's complement integer of width raw_bits.

section.name: Dual-Subframe Per Channel Architecture
section.t: When sample_type is float PCM (0b0001), each logical audio channel ch is represented using two subframes:

tr.td: Primary integer signal (FIXED, LPC, VERBATIM, or CONSTANT)
Packed lower mantissa bits (PACKED) or significand

section.t: A frame containing C channels contains 2 * C subframes.

section.name: Dynamic Positional Alignment (DPA) Mode
section.t: DPA mode is active when the Float Fallback Flag is 0.

The active bit position bounds across a frame for each channel are:
section.sourcecode: highest_pos = max_i(exp_i) lowest_pos = min_i(exp_i - 23 + ctz((1 << 23) | mant_i)) span = highest_pos - lowest_pos + 2
section.t: Given candidate upper bit depth B_upper (e.g., 24 bits) and lower bit depth B_lower = min(23, max(0, span - B_upper)):

section.name: Sample Reconstruction
section.t: To reconstruct IEEE 754 32-bit float samples:
section.sourcecode:
mask = (1 << lower_bits) - 1 if lower_bits > 0 else 0 base_exp = highest_exp - ((upper_bits + lower_bits) - 2)
for i in range(blocksize): up = upper_signal[i] low_val = lower_signal[i]
if up == 0: dest[i] = uint32_to_float(low_val) elif lower_bits == 0: sign = 1 if up < 0 else 0 uval = -up if up < 0 else up lead = ilog2(uval) shift = lead - 23 orig_exp = base_exp + lead explicit_mant = (uval >> shift if shift >= 0 else uval << (-shift)) dest[i] = compose_float(sign, orig_exp, explicit_mant & 0x7FFFFF) else: full_x = (up << lower_bits) | (low_val & mask) sign = 1 if full_x < 0 else 0 uval = -full_x if full_x < 0 else full_x lead = ilog2(uval) shift = lead - 23 orig_exp = base_exp + lead explicit_mant = (uval >> shift if shift >= 0 else uval << (-shift)) dest[i] = compose_float(sign, orig_exp, explicit_mant & 0x7FFFFF)

section.name: Fallback Mode
section.t: Fallback mode is active when the Float Fallback Flag is 1. It accommodates frames where the compressed bit count in DPA mode yields a compression ratio worse than or equal to 75% of uncompressed audio bits.

ol.li: Exponent Subframe (Subframe 2 * ch, 8 bits per sample):

li.t: Significand Subframe (Subframe 2 * ch + 1, 24 bits per sample):

section.t: Reconstruction in Fallback mode:
section.sourcecode:
orig_exp = (exp_signal[i] + 128) & 0xFF sm = sign_mant_signal[i]
if sm == -8388608: sign = 1 mant = 0 elif sm < 0: sign = 1 mant = (-sm) & 0x7FFFFF else: sign = 0 mant = sm & 0x7FFFFF
dest[i] = (sign << 31) | (orig_exp << 23) | mant

section.name: Inter-channel Decorrelation in Floating-Point Frames
section.t: When inter-channel decorrelation (Left-Side, Right-Side, or Mid-Side) is active in a stereo floating-point frame:

ul.li: In DPA Mode, decorrelation is applied exclusively to the Upper Subframes (Subframes 0 and 2). The side subframe receives bps + 1 bits resolution. The Lower Subframes (Subframes 1 and 3) remain independent.
In Fallback Mode, decorrelation is applied exclusively to the Exponent Subframes (Subframes 0 and 2).

section.name: Subframe Header Code Allocation
section.t: Section 9.2.1 of defines the 6-bit subframe type indicator. The code 0b000010 was previously reserved. This specification allocates 0b000010 to SUBFRAME_PACKED:

tr.td: MUST be 0 (wasted bits are not used for PACKED subframes)

section.name: PACKED Subframe Structure
section.t: The payload of a PACKED subframe directly follows the subframe header octet:

tr.td: 8-bit channel highest exponent / DC offset value
Sequence of blocksize variable-width bit sequences

section.name: Variable-Width Bit Truncation and Decoding Algorithm
section.t: The PACKED subframe carries lower-order mantissa bits associated with the integer signal decoded from the paired upper subframe (upper_subframe[i]).
For each sample i from 0 to blocksize - 1:

section.name: Ogg FLAC Encapsulation
section.t: When encapsulating FLAC streams containing STREAMINFO_EXTENSION in an Ogg container as specified in Section 10.1 of :

ul.li: The STREAMINFO_EXTENSION block constitutes an additional metadata header packet.
The 2-byte header packet count field in the first Ogg FLAC packet MUST account for STREAMINFO_EXTENSION in its total metadata packet count.

section.name: Cuesheets and CD-DA Constraints
section.t: In accordance with Compact Disc Digital Audio (CD-DA) constraints:

ul.li: The CD-DA subset flag in cuesheet metadata blocks MUST NOT be set if the audio stream uses floating-point sample format or has a sample rate other than 44,100 Hz.
For non-CD-DA cuesheet tracks on streams with fractional sample rates, sample offsets MUST be rounded to the nearest integer index using rint() rounding.

section.name: Seek Table Calculations with Float Sample Rates
section.t: Seek table target sample offsets and time-to-sample calculations MUST be computed using 64-bit IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point arithmetic when STREAMINFO_EXTENSION sample rate is present.

section.name: ReplayGain for Floating-Point Streams
section.t: ReplayGain analysis on 32-bit float streams operates directly on normalized floating-point samples (with reference level matching full-scale 1.0). During playback synthesis, gain adjustments are applied via direct linear float multiplication without integer quantization or hard clipping.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Implementations processing extended FLAC bitstreams must account for security considerations associated with untrusted audio decoding:

ol.li: Memory Allocation Validation: Channel counts up to 256 and bit depths up to 128 imply larger decoded frame buffers. Implementations MUST ensure that channel counts, block sizes, and bit depths declared in STREAMINFO_EXTENSION or Full Frame Headers do not cause integer overflows during buffer allocation calculations.

IEEE 754 Special Value Validation: Decoders MUST validate the 64-bit floating-point sample rate field in STREAMINFO_EXTENSION and frame headers. De-serialized double-precision values MUST be checked for subnormals, infinities, and NaN payloads to prevent undefined floating-point behavior, division-by-zero errors in timeline calculations, or denial-of-service conditions during seek operations.

Entropy Decoder Buffer Bounds: In PARTITIONED_RICE3, escape parameters signal unencoded raw bit lengths up to 127 bits. Bitstream readers MUST strictly verify buffer boundaries prior to variable-width bit consumption to prevent out-of-bounds memory reads.

Header CRC-8 Verification: Implementations MUST verify the frame header CRC-8 over the full extended header payload before attempting to interpret extended frame properties or allocate subframe resources.
